notes.title: Teamfight Tactics patch 18.3
notes.description: 18.3 is a more focused patch, with smaller, more specific changes to Champs/Traits as we nerf power ceilings, or bring up power floors, and broader buffs to combat Augments.
notes.html:
Buff struggling rerollers, squash bugs (not you Kha'Zix), and Enchant the Wilds!

18.3 is a medium-sized patch focused on giving new life to comps that may have appeared during PBE but haven't been found in the Wilds since—I'm looking at you Wolf Bros. Past balance, we've got a ton of bug fixes for this patch, split into two categories—gameplay, where we finally found those missing PvE fights, and stability/performance, where we added a fix to the Augment UI that could result in selecting an incorrect Augment. Oh, and we also have a few Wisp nerfs to the must-buys and buffs for our often-skipped Combat Augments. Let's get into it!

Rodger "Riot Prism" Caudill
Katie "Riot Ukime" Guo

PATCH HIGHLIGHTS

LARGE CHANGES

Large, like Brambleback's back.

TRAITS

As a splash with powerful units, Blossom (3) provides too much value for a few over-performing Wisps in particular. This change may look like a big nerf, cause there are a lot of lines, but the reality of gameplay here is that you'll typically only be impacted by 2-5 of these Wisp nerfs throughout a game in most cases.

As a high-stakes trait without the potential to be griefed, we released Coven with cashout generation that was more conservative than past high-stakes traits. We're increasing Loss Essence generation across most breakpoints here to bring Coven out of the dark.

Hunter, Defender, Invoker, and even Inferno nerfs are to the highest breakpoint of the traits, where powerful Emblems allow for too much value. We have a few more Emblem specific nerfs later on, but so as to not make the max breakpoints, nor the Emblems, useless, we've split the nerfs into two smaller parts.

  • Blossom Charms:
    • Animate Shop Duration: 26s ⇒ 24s
    • Blaze Damage: 1.5% max Health ⇒ 1.25% max Health
    • Blood Money Cost: 1g ⇒ 2g
    • Combust Damage: 22% ⇒ 18%
    • Curio Cart Bonus Gold: 2g ⇒ 1g
    • Heated Rivalry Takedowns: 7 ⇒ 5
    • Heroic Sacrifice AD/AP: 40% ⇒ 35%
    • Heroic Sacrifice Armor/MR: 40 ⇒ 35
    • Hugify Health: 600 ⇒ 500
    • Mana Rich Soil Reduction: 25% ⇒ 20%
    • Mercenary Force Damage Amp: 4.5% ⇒ 4%
    • Moonlight Ritual Cost: 2g ⇒ 3g
    • Sinister Deal Gold: 3g ⇒ 2g
    • Sinister Deal Health Lost: 3HP ⇒ 2HP
    • Stand Alone Health/Damage Amp: 22% ⇒ 20%
  • Coven Essence Per Loss: 18/25/32/60 ⇒ 22/28/35/60
  • Defender Resists: 25/60/120 ⇒ 25/60/115
  • Hunter Bonus AD: 20/30/45/65% ⇒ 20/30/40/60%
  • Inferno Burn Amount: 1/1/3.5/4.5% ⇒ 1/1/3/4%
  • Invoker Mana Regen: 3/4/6/9 ⇒ 3/4/6/8

UNITS: TIER 1

It's about time for Karma to get what she deserves: a buff across all star levels, but especially three-star, where she's yet to be seen as a mid-game reroll carry.

Unlike Karma, Ornn has been able to access Artifacts too easily with optimal set-ups. We're slowing three-star Ornn down, since he's been able to print these Artifacts for Solar comps to spike in the late game, while making sure our two-star Ornns ornn't griefed.

As a reroll carry, Veigar has found success with a few openers that can shore up his weak early game. Some of these set-ups lead to incredibly powerful Veigar carries that feel almost impossible to overcome, but if you want to add Veigar in for his traits, he's all but a dead unit. We're trimming a bit out of his power ceiling, so Veigar can be less of a dead unit when not played as the centerpiece of a comp. There's certainly three to eight potential short jokes for this context paragraph, but I feel like it's about time we stood above that. #shortkings(and queens)

  • Karma Explosion Damage: 120/180/270/460 AP ⇒ 125/185/300/515 AP
  • Ornn three-star Forge Power Bonus: +100% ⇒ +85%
  • Ornn 2nd Artifact Threshold: 155,000 Forge Power ⇒ 140,000 Forge Power
  • Veigar AP Per Kill: 3% ⇒ 2%
  • Veigar Ability Damage Base: 175/265/395/670 AP ⇒ 200/300/450/765 AP
  • Veigar Ability Damage Empowered: 265/400/595/1015 AP ⇒ 300/450/675/1015

UNITS: TIER 2

Alistar hasn't been much more than a big health bar when three-starred. He's getting a lot more damage in his ability and a more powerful heal to have this Elder bull feel like a younger pup.

Speaking of pups, the Wolf Bros are back to be your new favorite Level 6 reroll comp to play. Just remember to sacrifice an Attack Fighter and not a Tank for the Blackthorn Hex, and since we haven't seen Warwick in a while, be sure to grab a Titan's Resolve and Spear of Shojin, cause mana regen = ramping Attack Speed. As for Murkwolf, positioning, positioning, positioning… for you and your opponent.

Gromp is also getting a buff that should be more impactful to the AD form, but a nice buff to AP as well. Gromp and Murkwolf being buffed in the same patch may seem scary, since Riftbeast is not too far off, but most Riftbeast comps do not run both of these Units, especially as carries. Maybe that can change though?

  • Alistar Heal: 200/260/320 AP ⇒ 230/300/400 AP
  • Alistar Ability Damage: 100/150/225 AP ⇒ 180/270/420 AP
  • Gromp AP Form Ability DoT: 160/240/360 AP ⇒ 175/265/410 AP
  • Gromp AD Form Attack Speed: 0.7 ⇒ 0.75
  • Gromp AD Form Base AD: 45 ⇒ 50
  • Murkwolf Empowered Attack Damage: 60/90/135 AD ⇒ 65/100/160 AD
  • Warwick Ability Damage: 215/325/500 AD ⇒ 230/345/535 AD
  • Warwick Ability Healing: 20% ⇒ 25%

UNITS: TIER 3

With 6 Defender being nerfed, which was a huge source of stall power for Cassiopeia comps, we can put some power into Cassiopeia and Rammus directly so they can slither/roll into more than just 6 Defender comps.

Even in his prime, AP flex, tanky Blackthorn sacrifice, two-star Malphite era, Azir was never the go-to carry.

  • Azir Ability Damage: 43/65/103 ⇒ 46/69/110
  • Cassiopeia Ability Damage: 400/600/950 ⇒ 425/630/1020
  • Rammus Shield: 350/450/550 ⇒ 400/550/725

UNITS: TIER 4

Lillia's only go-to comps, Fae (4) + Cassiopeia Defender, aren't typically seen past 4th place, leaving this 4-cost tank without a home. With a solid buff to her healing, she may be able to survive enough for a second cast, sleeping more foes, and making her way into more comps as a utility tank.

Nidalee's AD form was gaining more Armor penetration than intended, but even with that fixed, she's still slightly over the line, so we've got a small nerf to the AD scaling on her swipe. And while AD Nidalee is our strongest 4-cost at the moment, AP Nidalee is rarely itemized, so we're giving her third attack, her snipe at the farthest enemy with the least items, a pointy buff.

  • Lillia Heal: 325/475 AP ⇒ 350/525 AP
  • Nidalee: Fixed a bug where Nidalee was gaining 60% Armor Penetration instead of 40% Armor Penetration
  • Nidalee AD form Ability Armor Penetration: 40% ⇒ 60% (no functional change)
  • Nidalee AD form Ability Damage: 225/340 AD ⇒ 210/315 AD
  • Nidalee AP Form Third Attack Damage: 300/450 AP ⇒ 330/500 AP

UNITS: TIER 5

Even when we tried to incentivize itemizing Taric last patch, he was still often skipped over by our premiere 4-cost tanks (or Maokai). We're polishing the Emerald Aspect's heal to make a bit of AP feel good on him, while taking away some of his passive team-wide shielding (which is a flat value unaffected by items).

  • Lux Solar Lux Bonus Damage per 3-star: 12% ⇒ 15%
  • Taric Passive Shield Base Value: 100/225 ⇒ 75/150
  • Taric Heal: 250/375 AP ⇒ 275/450 AP

ARTIFACTS

Draven with the Collector is absolutely terrifying, and it still will be, just a tiny bit less. But past Draven (and Aphelios), the Collector provides a lot of econ and combat power, making it one of the better Artifacts on the set, especially in the right hands.

Unlike The Collector, Statikk Shiv has yet to find consistent users apart from Kayle. A bit more Ability Power should make this item more appealing even in situations where it's dropped too late in the game to field Kayle.

  • The Collector AD: 40% ⇒ 35%
  • Eternal Pact Mana on Tank Ability Cast: 15 ⇒ 10
  • Statikk Shiv Base Ability Power: 15% ⇒ 25%

EMBLEMS

Smaller nerfs here (and one buff) as the traits that are enabled by our over-performing Emblems are also getting nerfed.

  • Brawler Emblem Damage: 2% max HP ⇒ 2.5% max HP
  • Hunter Emblem AD Per Takedown: 18% ⇒ 15%
  • Invoker Emblem Mana Regen: 3 ⇒ 2
  • Juggernaut Emblem Mana Restore on Death: 15 ⇒ 10

AUGMENTS

We've got a lot of Augment changes here, but for the most part they are buffs to combat Augments, which have been deprioritized with the emphasis on econ Augments this set.

One combat/Item Augment that was greatly buffed through our Hand of Justice buff last patch, Retribution, is getting a nerf to keep things feeling just with other combat Augments.

One last critical callout is that we renamed the empowered hex in the It's Me Baby Augment to be called the Championship hex instead of the Spotlight hex. Keep it up champ.

  • Bonus Gift Renamed Bonus Gifts
  • Blossom's Call Minimum Wisp Cost to see 4-cost By Stage: 15/6/4/0g ⇒ 15/5/3/0g
  • Blossom's Call Minimum Wisp Cost to see 4-cost By Stage: X/15/8/5/0 ⇒ X/15/8/4/0
  • Challenger's Grace Buff Duration: 3s ⇒ 4s
  • Early Learnings Baseline AD/AP: 5% ⇒ 3%
  • Electrocharge I Damage By Stage: 30/50/70/90 ⇒ 25/40/60/80
  • Infinity Protection Disabled due to a bug
  • Item Extraction Number of Extractions: 4 ⇒ 3
  • Item Extraction Now grants an additional Azir
  • It's Me, Baby Spotlight renamed to Championship Hex.
  • Feeling Lucky Flipping Heads no longer grants 4 more gold than intended
  • Frontline Foundation can now grant Yorick + Juggernaut emblem
  • Future Focused Gold: 8 ⇒ 5
  • Giant and Mighty Health: 200 ⇒ 225
  • Group Hug I Resists: 6 ⇒ 7
  • Group Hug II Resists: 9 ⇒ 10
  • Heroic Grab Bag Initial Gold: 4g ⇒ 6g
  • Hold the Line AD: 9% ⇒ 11%
  • Hold the Line AP: 10% ⇒ 11%
  • Jeweled Lotus I Crit Chance: 10% ⇒ 15%
  • Retribution Crit Chance: 25% ⇒ 15%
  • Shimmerscale Essence Round Delay: 8 ⇒ 6
  • Shimmerscale Essence First Item is now Gambler's Blade
  • Shimmerscale Essence Second Item is now Mogul's Mail
  • Spirit of Redemption Heal: 7.5% ⇒ 9%
  • Upward Mobility Reroll On Level: 1 ⇒ 2
  • Verticality now requires at least 4 units of a trait to be offered
  • We Stick Together: Can't give the same emblem to multiple players; can't give emblems for traits that are too small; can't give emblems for Juggernaut, Brawler, or Defender
  • Weight the Worth no longer grants a Tiny Duplicator

WISPS

These Wisps are too spirited, too much value, too wispy, too thingamajigy.

  • Stat Boosters Armor and MR Boost: 10 ⇒ 8
  • Stat Boosters Attack Speed Boost: 8% ⇒ 6%
  • Blood and Iron Cost: 3g ⇒ 4g
  • Combust Explosion Damage: 18% ⇒ 15%
  • Mana-Rich Soil Mana Reduction: 18% ⇒ 15%
  • Thingamajig Wisps Less likely to grant Mana Regen Boosters.
  • Three Me Cost: 9g ⇒ 10g

BUG FIXES

  • Worth The Wait can no longer give the same Champion to multiple players
  • Craftable and uncraftable emblems can now be reforged into each other
  • Getting the Golden Egg from Call to Chaos with a full bench no longer fails to grant the egg

  • Fixed an issue where Pandora's Bench would take/return double the units from the available champion pool. For example if you roll a two-star Sett into a two-star Aphelios, instead of being +3/-3 copies moving in the pool it would be +6 and then -6. As long as you kept rolling the pool would fix itself and return to normal, but it would temporarily alter pool contents.

PERFORMANCE/STABILITY BUG FIXES

notes.title: Teamfight Tactics patch 18.2
notes.description: It’s the first main patch of Enchanted Wilds and we’ve got a patch full of buffs to bring some of our struggling comps out from under the canopy. Along with a bunch of buffs we’re taking a huge pass at lowering the cost of our Wisps so you can keep your gold to buy XP or keep rolling for that last copy of Master Yi.
notes.html:
It’s our first main patch for Enchanted Wilds, but if you’ve missed the several mid-patch updates for 18.1, you can always catch up on those changes here; there were a lot. As for this patch, our focus is on continuing to squash bugs, with more bugfixes and performance improvements planned for the next few patches. On the gameplay side, we’re enabling comps that haven’t had the chance to shine under the canopy of reroll and Ahri, while also making some small adjustments to the economy to support leveling to 8, 9, and 10 via direct cost reductions per level and cheaper combat Wisps throughout the game. As they say, more gold in the bank, more chances to miss in your rolldown.

Rodger "Riot Prism" Caudill
Katie "Riot Ukime" Guo

MID-PATCH UPDATE

SEPTEMBER 14

18.2 set out to enable fast 9 strategies amidst a reroll-heavy meta of 18.1, but through more econ via cheaper Wisps, lower leveling costs, and powerful buffs, Legendary-soup variations quickly shifted what S-tier stands for.

SYSTEMS

Our 18.2 changes to XP reduced the cost of going to Level 10 by 12 gold—that’s a lot in the world of TFT, especially when you’re saving anywhere from 5-15 gold on cheaper Wisps. We’re not doing a total revert of the XP changes here, as we’re keeping it cheaper to go from Level 7 to 8 by 4 XP/gold, but 9 and 10 are getting their changes reverted.

  • XP From Level 8-9: 64 ⇒ 68
  • XP From Level 9-10: 64 ⇒ 68

AUGMENTS

As expected, Expected Unexpectedness has been re-enabled, but a newly unexpected bug has had us pull Nesting Dolls temporarily.

  • Expected Unexpectedness Re-enabled
  • Nesting Dolls Disabled due to a bug

UNITS

Camille has found her place as a powerful reroll carry in Solar/Ravager boards even in a meta that leans towards fast 9. Since we’re nerfing all our Level 9/10 comps and a few more pricey units, we’re pre-emptively delivering a weightier nerf for our best performing reroll comps.

LeBlanc is still being used as more of a reroll printer than a unit that sticks around on end-game boards. We’re lowering her base chance to print at three-stars, but as an itemized carry she should still be pretty consistent as a champ printer since the bonus chance via takedowns is unchanged.

notes.html:
Welcome to the Enchanted Wilds!

Take a walk through a forest full of powerful protectors of nature, whimsical Wisps, and Traits for the various parts of the Wilds. This is going to be a big patch doc, focused on the existing systems (Items, Carousel (it's back), Encounters, etc), but for more information about our set be sure to check out the Enchanted Wilds Overview and our Enchanted Wilds Dev Drop.

As a reminder, we're keeping Space Gods, set 17, on for a few patches longer, so we also have a small balance update there. We've also been yapping quite frequently during the Enchanted Wilds' PBE, so if you missed our latest update on moving from PBE to live, be sure to catch it here.

Katie "Riot Ukime" Guo
Rodger "Riot Prism" Caudill

Mid-Patch Updates

AUGUST 31ST AND SEPTEMBER 1ST

Our third mid-patch update will be rolling out August 31st for the balance changes and September 1st for bug fixes and quality of life improvements.

TRAITS

Riftbeast (7) has proven to be a super consistent trait whether you’re sitting there to star up your 1-costs, or pushing levels to slot in flexible Legendary units.

  • Riftbeast (7) Stats: 6% AD/AP/AS ⇒ 5% AD/AP/AS

CHAMPIONS

Drop Pebbles, Cinderling stocks are on fire! Through optimized builds, and consistency of starring this little guy up via Riftbeast shops, Cinderling’s ramped up as a powerful carry. We’ve got a base AD and ability nerf to keep him in check and give Pebbles fans a more equal footing.

Cassiopeia Defender is one of the most consistent comps of our patch. We’re taking a big chunk out of the main damage threat here.

Master Yi is another reroll star that’s become a powerhouse, especially with an Artifact or two. We’re lowering his defenses to keep this melee-carry burstable.

Amumu has had a lot to cry about with our release patch. Let’s cheer him up with a double buff.

Draven’s our worst performing 5-cost by a considerable amount. We’re swinging big with a buff to allow him to cast much sooner and take advantage of more bleeds being built up. Attack Speed, which was already his best stat, is going to be even better, so grab those bows!

  • Cinderling Base AD: 45 ⇒ 40
  • Cinderling Ability Damage: 340/510/765/1300 AD ⇒ 310/465/700/1200 AD
  • Cassiopeia Ability Damage: 440/660/1050 AP ⇒ 400/600/950 AP
  • Master Yi Resists: 60 ⇒ 55
  • Ahri Ability Damage: 450/675 AP ⇒ 425/640 AP
  • Amumu Mana buff: 30/140 ⇒ 30/125
  • Amumu Heal Max HP %: 2.2% ⇒ 2.5%
  • Morgana Mana nerf: 0/60 ⇒ 0/65
  • Soraka Initial Star Damage: 190/285 AP ⇒ 225/335 AP
  • Draven Mana buff: 0/120 ⇒ 0/110
  • Draven Base AS: 0.8 ⇒ 0.85
  • Elder Dragon Base AD: 115 ⇒ 125
  • Lux Ability Damage: 330/520 AP ⇒ 355/550 AP
  • Lux Lunar Damage Amp: 10% ⇒ 8%

GAME FEEL AND PERFORMANCE

Note that these changes will be patched separately tomorrow, September first in the early evening. Alongside a few gameplay-related bugfixes we also have a quality of life, or game feel, adjustment for dragging and dropping units to allow for more reactive/snappier unit movement. This should be most noticeable when using the units on your bench as a virtual fidget spinner.

Update: we discovered some unintended bugs related to the flushing system below so ahead of release, we'll be pushing it back to a future patch.

In our effort to continue to improve performance across devices, we’ve put in a medium-term fix that “flushes” particles when they build up. This is just one of the fixes we plan on rolling out to improve performance, but this fix should specifically help reduce instances where you experience worsening performance as you get into the later stages of a game. Impact may vary depending on your device specs, but we'll continue to roll out fixes over the next few patches to continue improving here.

  • Game Feel: Champion Drag and Drop snappiness has been improved
  • Late Game Performance: Upgraded our particle flusher tool to boost performance on round transitions and Carousel

BUGS

Note that these changes will be patched separately tomorrow, September first in the early evening.

  • Maladaptive: Using an Item Remover on a starred-up Adaptor no longer swaps them back to their one-star scaling
  • Players can no longer repeatedly fight a ghost army multiple rounds in a row
  • Alune’s ability can no longer target untargetable units
  • Certain Adaptor units no longer revert to a their alternate form’s Mana costs
  • Master of All Origins now has proper Icons
  • Augment Pillars no longer have white boxes appearing in the icon right after acquiring an Augment
  • Double Up: Upgraded Life Debt wisps now properly eliminates players. Maybe don’t buy it at 1 HP.
  • Double Up: Final Showdown Encounter now properly gives the two final duos 70 gold

AUGUST 28TH

NEW FEATURE

With load times longer than we wanted with our release, we’ve added a spinning graphic in the loading screen to reduce paranoia around whether or not it is a crash or just a longer loading screen. Even with loading times coming down since release, we still want this around and are still working on future optimization.

  • Added a spinner graphic to pre-match loading screens for all platforms.

DOUBLE UP

We’re moving fast and hard here to ship as many bug fixes and performance improvements as possible, but in our eagerness to do so, a new bug emerged yesterday resulting in us temporarily disabled the Double Up queue. It’s back now, so grab your Double Up pal and let em’ know.

  • Double Up has been reenabled.
  • Fixed an exploit where temporary items would become permanent if traded with the friendship cannon.

BUG FIXES

  • Fixed an issue with a few ability/action instances such as Elise’s transformation, Maokai’s death, Sejuani’s weapon swipe, Sentinel’s Idle VFX, and Tristana’s AOE Explosion having memory leaks.
  • Fixed a temporary delay in joining queues on Mobile
  • Fixed memory leak of particles in Arena Prancie’s Retreat
  • MOBILE: Fixed an issue where the “Update Available” modal would in rare instances kick a player from Mobile on certain devices
  • Fixed an issue where Loot orbs would pop-in later than their trailing VFX when dropping from a minion in a PvE round
  • Temporarily Disabled Forge A Friend Augment as it wasn’t consistently providing a three-star unit.
  • MOBILE: Fixed an issue where some Mobile devices were running TFT in settings that surpassed their hardware recommendations resulting in poor performance
  • Fixed an issue where Health Bar subticks rendered too wide
  • Fixed an issue with Default Key functions
  • MOBILE: Fixed an issue where the “Update Available” modal was unable to be interacted with on certain Mobile devices
  • Fixed a bug where Teemo’s mushroom loot could land outside the board on certain Arenas after casting his ability during combat
  • Prestige Shyvana will now properly play her Dragon Form boom while in Dragon form
  • Change from Vulcan to OpenGL for specific GPUs to reduce graphics related crashes
  • Changing the default quality settings for some devices that were performing poorly

AUGUST 27TH

The team’s out with our first round of bug fixes targeting high priority bugs from memory leaks that cause performance issues to Finishers not abiding by global volume/sfx settings (they were loud).

While this is our first mid-patch update we expect to have another follow up soon with more bugs squashed and a check-in on live balance as the meta evolves.

BUG FIXES

  • Fixed a memory leak with the Golden Egg asset
  • Fixed a memory leak that could happen when playing Rengar, which could lead to performance issues over time.
  • Fixed the End of Game screen sometimes showing the wrong final placement for the players who finished 1st and 2nd in Ranked games.
  • Fixed the "Soul Awakening" Augment's True Damage only working on Attack Damage instead of also applying to Ability Damage.
  • Fixed a bug where changing your loadout in TFT could accidentally unequip items from your League of Legends loadout.
  • Fixed a localization bug on mobile where the Performance Mode graphics setting showed English text instead of your selected language.
  • Fixed the "Bobabear" section of the Tacticians loadout screen showing untranslated (English-only) text.
  • Fixed some in-progress cosmetic category titles and item names showing in English regardless of your language setting.
  • Fixed a matchmaking issue that could cause you to face the same opponent two rounds in a row.
  • Fixed combat sometimes failing to end properly when Gnar knocked a Krug off the board.
  • Fixed Little Legend finisher sound effects continuing to play even after turning Global Volume/SFX down to 0.
  • Fixed the scoreboard constantly shifting position when purchasing Charms.
  • Fixed a bug preventing players from opening Settings
  • Fixed overlapping music tracks playing at the same time.
  • Improved Kennen's AOE visual effects so they scale better on lower graphics settings.
  • Improvements to Performance Mode for lower-spec devices to help maintain frame rate.
  • Fixed some load time related issues.
  • Fixed several minor memory leak sources.

ENCHANTED WILDS RELEASE PERFORMANCE NOTES

Patch 18.1 is our first foray into the Enchanted Wilds on live with our transition from Hextech to Unreal. With the new engine, it's taking time for us to get up to speed, reach parity, and eventually, accelerate into the full potential of our new engine. With that in mind, there are going to be some very noticeable differences between set 17 and 18 that we are actively working to close the gap on.

  • Bugs: With a new set going live, there are always a few bugs to be found with the millions of games occurring in just the opening hours of a set. With a new engine, we expect that few to be more than usual, but as with PBE, we're actively working on fixing them, so as always please report any bugs you come across using community social spaces, support tickets, or the client.
  • Loading Times: Upon launch, loading into Enchanted Wilds will take longer than normal. We thank you for your patience during these load screens, and we are working on the back-end to reduce them.
  • Pings and Mini-map: You may notice that the mini-map is gone, and with it, pings are MIA. With the minimap gone, we still want to preserve the strategic (or humorous) communications from Pings, so we're taking Pings into the shop to rework them into a social tool that's not bound to the minimap. This will take some time and won't be ready on release, but we'll ping you when we've got a clearer understanding of their release timing.
  • Friend spectate on Live is something that we know is important for community super-contributors, community events, and just hanging out with your pals. It’s something we will not have on launch, but is on the docket to release long-term with the intention of a better spectator experience overall.
  • Patch Size: 18.1 is going to be big on the data size side of things, and the game side of things—it is a new set… Expect future patches to be smaller in size after our initial release.
  • Finishers: As we port our entire catalogue of Tacticians, Arenas, Booms, and Emotes over to Unreal, the trickiest aspect of our transition has been bringing over Finishers. As a temporary solution to speed up this process, we’re displaying Finishers as a video rather than in engine. Until Finishers are rebuilt in engine, they’ll be performed on River Sprites.
  • Cosmetics: Migrating all our cosmetics over from Hextech to Unreal is going to take some time. Each patch we plan on adding more and more cosmetics until we’ve achieved parity. For a detailed list of the Cosmetics available on release, please see the section at the end of these notes.

TFT MINIMUM SPECS

We're keeping our minimum specifications fairly similar on Mobile, with the exception of iOS 2GB & Android 2/3 GB devices, which make up a pretty small portion of global devices with TFT installed. As for PC, our minimum specifications are Windows 10 (Version 19041+), DirectX11 (Feature Level 4.3), and Shader Model 5.

VICTORIOUS LUMIE

For those of you who achieved Gold or higher in Space Gods Ranked or Double up, great job! There'll be a very excited Lumie to herald your victory!

SYSTEMS

SET MECHANIC: WISPS

For a detailed dive into Wisps mechanic make sure you check out the Enchanted Wilds Overview. For now, here are some highlights.

  • Wisps are split into 7 Categories (Champion, Combat, Misc, Shop, Gold/XP, Risky, Item). These categories have distinct coloring and icons to make rolling down and scouting as their icon will appear by a player's Tactician HP bar upon purchase.
  • Wisps can only be purchased during the planning phase. After the planning phase, the Wisp will be whisked away, revealing the unit that was hiding behind it.
  • Wisps appear in every other shop.
  • After stage 5, every other Wisp is guaranteed to be a Combat Wisp.

CAROUSEL

  • The Carousel has returned!
  • Carousel now has a chance to contain more champions and/or champions with a higher costs than normal.

TARGETING

In hextech, units were hardcoded to retarget after being CC'd (stunned, knocked-up), targeting the closest enemy to them. This meant if a backliner was hit by an AOE stun, they'd retarget whoever is closest to them'bad luck if you're an assassin that's snuck into the backline. With Set 18, we're able to do away with this awkward retargeting as CC will no longer be accompanied by target amnesia.

  • Units will no longer retarget after returning from Crowd Control.

PVE LOOT

Pro-tip: You still shouldn't miss loot at Stage 4-7.

  • Missed loot from Stage 4-7, or later PVE rounds, can now overflow to the next PVE round.

OPENING ENCOUNTERS

We're removing a few Opening Encounters that were too warping, while adding some more standard-style Encounters to keep lower impact variance varied. We've played with high and low impact Opening Encounters for a while now, and, especially in a set like 18, there doesn't need to be such extreme highs in variance with this system, as much of the game to game variance comes instead from Wisps, Augments, Item distribution, and what units you see in the shop.

notes.description: It’s our final dedicated patch for Space Gods before Enchanted Wilds arrives on live.
notes.html:
It’s our final dedicated patch for Space Gods before Enchanted Wilds arrives on live. Note that, for those of you dedicated to space travel, you’ll still be able to play Space Gods even when Enchanted Wilds is live for a limited period. So for this final dedicated patch we’ve got some fun and exciting twists to keep space, the place.

Rodger "Riot Prism" Caudill
Katie "Riot Ukime" Guo

PATCH HIGHLIGHTS

ENCHANTED WILDS

Our newest set, Enchanted Wilds, will go live at the end of patch 17.9, on August 26th. To learn more about the set, check out our latest Dev Drop, or shorter bite-sized content.

  • Dev Drop: Enchanted Wilds
  • TFT Enchanted Wilds in 60 Seconds
  • TFT Set 18's Mechanic: Wisps!
  • The Wildest 5-costs of Set 18

LARGE CHANGES

Large, like the verdant forest of Wisps and new champions to find in the Enchanted Wilds.

TRAITS

Giving some love to the Shepherd so the summon can feel more impactful, casting more often, scaling more throughout the fight, and have a powerful Shepherd (7) damage impact.

  • Shepherd Mana buff: 0/50 ⇒ 0/40
  • Shepherd AP Per Cast: 15 ⇒ 10
  • Shepherd Summon Shield Duration: 4s ⇒ 3s
  • Shepherd Tail Sweep Damage: 200/230/275 AP ⇒ 200/300/400 AP
  • Shepherd 7 Shepherd Wave Damage: 220 AP ⇒ 300 AP

UNITS: TIER 1

It’s all in the heart of the cards. Twisted Fate will now have much higher high-rolls and much weaker (and tilting) low-rolls.

  • Twisted Fate now always grants gold if a 9 is rolled, regardless of star level. If a 1 is rolled, Twisted Fate takes 15% max health true damage.
  • Twisted Fate Minimum Damage: 200/305/460/800 AP ⇒ 30/45/70/120 AP
  • Twisted Fate Maximum Damage: 450/675/1015/1725 AP ⇒ 680/1020/1550/2650 AP

UNITS: TIER 2

Through partial reworks and big buffs we’re creating new high damage carries or just making sure Gwen can cut above the B-tier.

By adopting her Champion Augment into her base ability, Meepsie is channeling her inner DIVE, truly going out with a bang, bang, bang, bang.

  • Gwen Groove Threshold: 40% ⇒ 50%
  • Gwen Primary Target Damage: 145/220/410 AP ⇒ 155/235/440 AP
  • Milio has a 40% chance to cast an additional time at an additional target that can also bounce to new targets.
  • Milio Primary Spell Damage: 255/380/575 AP ⇒ 200/300/470 AP
  • Milio Bounce Damage: 85/130/190 AP ⇒ 60/90/150 AP
  • Meepsie Role: Magic Tank ⇒ Magic Fighter
  • Meepsie Mana: 50/100 ⇒ 0/55
  • Meepsie Base AD: 65 ⇒ 20
  • Meepsie Base AS: 0.55 ⇒ 0.65
  • Meepsie Spell Replaced with Champion Augment’s “Big Bang”
  • Meepsie Passive Damage: 40/60/90 AP ⇒ 30/45/70 AP
  • Meepsie Spell Damage: 240/360/560 AP ⇒ 180/270/425 AP
  • Meepsie Bonus Passive Damage Per Meep: 60% ⇒ 50%
  • Meepsie Stun Duration: 1.25/1.5/1.75s ⇒ 1/1/1.5s

UNITS: TIER 3

More Gold, more Attack Speed, more Damage.

Whether you’re printing gold with reroll Lulu, or giving your Rhaast a Sterak’s to become the AD Bruiser you know from Summoner’s Rift… anything is rhaasstible.

  • Lulu Medallion Gold Dropped: 1/3/5 ⇒ 1/4/7
  • Maokai Base Attack Speed: 0.6 ⇒ 0.7
  • Maokai NOVA Selector Max Health Damage: 8% ⇒ 12%
  • Rhaast Spell Duration: 2s ⇒ 1s
  • Rhaast Spell Damage: 120/180/300 AD ⇒ 400/600/1000 AD

UNITS: TIER 4

Annnnnd even more gold.

  • Tahm Kench Oracle gold per round increased

UNITS: TIER 5

If you still haven’t played Zed yet by somehow low rolling your Augments all set, this is your best chance to change that. Zed’s formally entered the set, but with his entrance we’re giving him a decent sized nerf due to his newfound availability.

  • Zed Added to the base champion roster

notes.title: Enchanted Wilds Overview
notes.description: Learn about Wisps and most of the new traits found in the Enchanted Wilds!
notes.html:
Make your way through the Enchanted Wilds, a set full of life from the summons of Elderwood, to the varied and helpful Wisps. Here we’ll go over some of the big verticals that comprise much of this forest and explore how Wisps work. So get ready to enter the Enchanted Wilds with our overview before the set goes live with patch 18.1 on August 26th!

WISPS

Wisps are an updated version of our Charms mechanic from Set 12, Magic N’ Mayhem, with quite a few quality-of-life changes and an all-new, adorable, dare-I-say enchanting, visual appearance.

Not sure what Charms or Wisps do? Here's a quick refresher: Wisps appear in your shop as temporary single-use sources of power in Combat, for resources like XP or gold, or even risky deals with conniving forest denizens.

You can purchase one Wisp per round, and it’ll appear in every other shop. Wisps will always appear in the rightmost slot, with most lasting just one round. As the game progresses, Wisps tend to get more powerful. And more powerful Wisps also cost more!

notes.html:
It's a Legendary patch full of buffs!

But the buffest one of all is Choncc (believe you me, Choncc's all muscle), who's bringing back Set 16, Lore & Legends, in his own Choncc style (Choncc's Treasure). But looking past our favorite pink (or whatever color of variant you run Choncc in) dragon is a patch full of all buffs and adjustments (and one nerf), so read on as Vex joins the Stargazers and Shen changes the timeline.

Rodger "Riot Prism" Caudill
Katie "Riot Ukime" Guo

PATCH HIGHLIGHTS

ENCHANTED WILDS

We're hard at work on our next set, Enchanted Wilds, which will go to PBE on July 28th. To learn more about the set check out our latest Dev Drop, or shorter bite-sized content.

CHONCC'S LORE & LEGENDS

Starting this patch, Set 16 will return with Choncc's Lore & Legends! It's Choncc's Treasure on a set that brought all (ehh, most) of Runeterra to life with Unlockables. So take a trip down memory lane with the limited mode!

  • Choncc's Treasure on Lore & Legends goes live shortly after the patch deploys
  • Brings back Set 16's roster with Choncc's Treasure's fun-fueled loot

MOBILE MINIMUM SPEC CHANGES

As we continually develop Teamfight Tactics, we occasionally update the minimum system requirements to continue playing. Starting July 22nd, we'll be ending support for 2GB/3GB mobile devices. Players on these devices will need to upgrade in order to continue to play TFT on mobile.

ESPORTS

The Tactician’s Crown has concluded, and a new global champion has been crowned. Congratulations to NAME REDACTED FOR THOSE WHO WANNA WATCH THE VODS for earning the favor of the Space Gods and making history as the best TFT player in the world during Set 17.

Watch the finals VOD here and stay up to date with @CompeteTFT on X. Don’t forget to claim your Compete Card at competetft.com, and stay tuned for more details as Set 18 approaches.

LARGE CHANGES

Large, like the patch full of buffs ahead of us!

TRAITS

Anima Squad (6) is an exciting drip econ trait that turns your journey to the trait into a steady infusion of econ power. But it's not much of a journey if you just die before you can stabilize your board. We're bringing the trait down to a (5) piece, meaning you can now hit it without an Emblem, but more importantly, you can access it early with an Emblem. This'll be a huge buff for the trait, so we're also lowering the power of the rewards across the board.

Replicator (2) has seen a lot of success in pro play, but did you know there was a Replicator (4)? The trait's pretty hard to work into a comp as a (4) piece, so we're giving it a sizable buff to help it get onto boards near you.

Similar to Replicator, Rogue's never been a class worth investing deeply into—perhaps it's because of the unit's roguish loner nature, but more likely because going deep into the trait means missing out on core tank/utility units.

Lastly, we've got a nerf for Timebreaker (4), which is now easier to hit with Shen changing the timelines and gaining it as an Origin. We'll talk more about just this, but if you want to time travel, you can just scroll faster to Units: Tier 5.

  • Anima Squad Trait Breakpoint: 3/6 ⇒ 3/5
  • Anima Squad Max Breakpoint Rewards:
    • 2 5-costs + 5g ⇒ 2 5-costs + 1g
    • Voyager Emblem + 3g ⇒ Voyager Emblem
    • Challenger Emblem + 5g ⇒ Challenger Emblem + 1g
    • 2x Lesser Champ Duplicator + 5g ⇒ 2x Lesser Champion Duplicator
    • Random Component + 5g ⇒ Random Component + 2g
  • Replicator Spell Effectiveness: 22/45% ⇒ 22/50%
  • Rogue AD/AP: 12/25/40/55% ⇒ 12/25/45/60%

UNITS: TIER 1

Ezreal's going to acquire additional drones faster which should bring his reroll fantasy into reality. Alongside a new Timebreaker in the line-up we expect to see a higher, and different cap to his board.

Talon is great early game, but he falls off faster and more than our other 1-costs. We're giving him more damage at three and four-stars to bring him up to the par of our lowest cost units (1-costs), but that doesn't make us value them any less.

  • Ezreal Takedowns Per Drone: 8 ⇒ 7
  • Talon Spell Damage AD: 400/600/1000/1700 ⇒ 400/600/1100/1850

UNITS: TIER 2

While we have seen Zoe in a few meta comps, TFT's best celestial ping pong player has never been the supreme carry in a comp. It's time to serve up a buff!

  • Zoe Secondary Spell Damage AP: 34/51/77 ⇒ 36/54/88 AP

UNITS: TIER 3

Urgot had one patch of reroll dominance early on in Space Gods, but this unstoppable dreadnought has been feeling rather stoppable since his decline. A decent AD buff should bring back his Sword-heavy carry builds.

  • Diana Shield AP: 275/325/475 ⇒ 275/325/515 AP, Spell Damage AP: 60/90/145 ⇒ 60/90/160 AP
  • Urgot Transformed Passive Damage: 225% AD ⇒ 250% AD

UNITS: TIER 4

Master Yi is our worst-performing 4-cost, so we're giving him a Mana buff that should have him entering his Psi-State (where he attacks and moves faster) earlier and with less down time.

  • Master Yi Mana: 30/70 ⇒ 20/60

UNITS: TIER 5

With 17.7 we're taking a bigger swing on making sure our Legendary units feel Legendary. Starting with Graves, who is having ALL his upgrades reduced to 1 gold. This should make him less of an econ burden and allow you to upgrade him whichever way you see fit.

We're also updating Shen with a new look and Origin trait, Timebreaker. A long time ago (during early iterations of the set), Shen was a Timebreaker, but we made him more of a flexible splashable Threat-like unit on release to allow for more comps that rolled into him to add him. With the return of his Origin trait we don't expect him to be less splashable—he still has the same power and utility as last patch—but we do expect to see a new high-cap for him as a Timebreaker carry. The trait will give him lots of Attack Speed, which he loves, so now you'll be able to itemize with more damage or survivability to create a new cap for this Timeline breaking trait.

Speaking of new traits, we've got another 5-cost getting one too, but don't get too excited, we know she wouldn't. Vex is getting a new look to join the Stargazer roster. This is going to be a considerable buff to her, especially since many Vex comps already run Nunu for frontline. So to go along with this big buff, we've got a compensation nerf to keep Vex from rising above her Shadow.

Finally, we're returning Zed to his past power. While the numbers are going down, those are percentage HP penalties, meaning Zed's clones will be slightly tankier than before.

  • Graves Upgrade Costs all reduced to 1
  • Shen New Trait: Timebreaker
  • Shen Skin updated
  • Vex New Trait: Stargazer
  • Vex Skin Updated
  • Vex Active Spell Damage: 140/210 AP ⇒ 130/195 AP
  • Zed Health Penalty: 33/45% ⇒ 33/40%

AUGMENTS

While Vex and Timebreaker are getting nerfs, they're mostly getting adjusted or buffed with the new additions to their kits/play patterns. The only ACTUAL nerf of this patch is for Birthday Reunion, an Augment that continues to outperform despite our nerf last patch.

Other than that single nerf, we've got a patch full of buffs for our most fun and set specific Augments. So chase that Apex Primordian or Nasus stacking dream!

  • Bonk! Base AS: 0.75 ⇒ 0.8

notes.title: Teamfight Tactics patch 17.6
notes.description: Patch 17.6 brings an update to Pengu’s Party and a balance pass on Space Gods with an Augment focus.
notes.html:
Welcome back party people!

Patch 17.6 is a smaller patch with a few buffs, specific nerfs, and a sweeping pass on Augments. The balance of the set is in a good spot right now, and we don’t want to shake too much up ahead of our regional tournaments. But where things are shaking up is Pengu’s Party, which has quite a few balance changes to keep the party going!

This will be a three week long patch (one week longer than usual), with 17.7 coming on July 15th to allow Rioters to take a week long break.

Rodger "Riot Prism" Caudill
Katie "Riot Ukime" Guo

PATCH HIGHLIGHTS

MOBILE MINIMUM SPEC CHANGES

As we continually develop Teamfight Tactics, we occasionally update the minimum system requirements to continue playing. Starting July 22nd, we’ll be ending support for 2GB/3GB mobile devices. Players on these devices will need to upgrade in order to continue to play TFT on mobile.

LARGE CHANGES

Large, like the announcement we made about migrating to Unreal.

TRAITS

Anima (6) is back on the buff list, this time with a small, but focused buff to ensure you’re able to spike faster with your initial rewards.

We’ve also got a few Arbiter buffs for the combos that are feeling a bit Arbitrary.

One of the biggest winners of last patch was reroll Gnar, which didn’t actually stay at Level 6 to slow roll for long. Instead, Gnar enjoyers opted to play for Levels after collecting enough Gnars, and then print the rest with Meeple (7). We don’t think Gnar is that far off in terms of balance, but the consistency of this comp is held together by its access to Level 9 through Meeple’s econ rewards. We’re shipping a small and targeted econ nerf here for Meeple (7), and going light on the Gnar nerf in an effort to keep the comp viable without the consistent dominance.

N.O.V.A. has a few fun fantasies with the Striker Selector, but too few of them haven’t been viable. We’re shipping buffs to the least selected, so keep your eyes out for new N.O.V.A. carries that’ll change the acronym to Nerf Overdue Very Appealing. Okay, not likely to take them into a “need nerf now” situation, but you try making an acronym out of N.O.V.A.

With our Shepherd AP nerf in our mid-patch update for 17.5 we’re able to move more power into the Summon itself and a few of the carries found in Shepherd comps. This should result in a much stronger summon, especially at Shepherd (7).

  • Anima Squad (6)
    • 15g cashout removed
    • 3x 4-cost cashout removed
    • 2x Lesser Duplicator ⇒ 2x Lesser Duplicator + 5g
    • More likely to receive Component/Emblem rewards
  • Arbiter Input - Rerolled Last Turn:
    • Gain Attack Speed: 35/55% ⇒ 40/65%
    • Gain Resists: 45/70 ⇒ 55/80
    • Gain Shield: 44/66% ⇒ 48/70%
    • Gain Gold: 30% ⇒ 35%
  • N.O.V.A (5) Bonuses:
    • Caitlyn Headshot Damage: 40% ⇒ 50%
    • Akali Damage: 12/18/24/30% AD ⇒ 15/22/28/34% AD
    • Kindred Damage Amp: 10% ⇒ 15%
  • Arbiter Output: Combat Start Shield Duration: 8s ⇒ 10s
  • Meeple (7) Gold per 2-cost Cloned: 5 ⇒ 3
  • Mecha AD/AP: 25/45/35% ⇒ 25/40/40%
  • Shepherd (5) Tail Sweep Damage: 200 AP ⇒ 230 AP
  • Shepherd (5) Health Multiplier (Stage 4-6): 6.5/7.25/8.5x ⇒ 6.75/7.8/9.5x
  • Shepherd (7) Shield: 430 AP ⇒ 460 AP
  • Shepherd (7) Tail Sweep Damage: 200 AP ⇒ 275 AP
  • Shepherd (7) Health Multiplier (Stage 4-6): 6.5/7.45/9.5x ⇒ 6.75/8/10x

UNITS: TIER 1

As our only champion that rolls dice and deals cards, Twisted Fate has found himself low-rolling and drawing bricks—which should hit hard, no? We’re giving him some much-needed buffs that’ll hopefully return him to a board, card table, or gambler’s den near you.

  • Twisted Fate Min Ability Damage AP: 190/285/430/730 ⇒ 205/305/460/800
  • Twisted Fate Max Ability Damage AP: 380/570/860/1460 ⇒ 410/610/920/1565

UNITS: TIER 2

With a targeted Meeple (7) nerf for the Gnar reroll comp, we’re able to go light with our nerf here.

Mordekaiser and a Heat Death (Champion Augment) buff in one patch!?

  • Gnar Base AD: 50 ⇒ 48
  • Mordekaiser Initial Shield: 350/425/550 ⇒ 350/450/625
  • Mordekaiser Shield Channel: 75/90/105 ⇒ 75/100/115

UNITS: TIER 3

Our 3-costs are all very close in terms of balance, but Viktor’s Psionic Storm is just a tad under the weather.

  • Viktor Ability Damage: 190/290/500 ⇒ 200/300/530
  • Lulu Altar Spell Damage: 150/225/375 AP ⇒ 160/240/400 AP
  • Lulu Serpent Spell Damage: 140/210/335 AP ⇒ 150/225/360 AP

UNITS: TIER 4

With Shepherd’s AP share in check, we’re able to buff Karma and LeBlanc in hopes they can find homes in their AP Shepherd flex lines and others alike.

As a Threat-like tank, if Morgana can’t do the tanking, she’s just a nice passive trait for your team. With more HP gain and ally healing, this Dark Lady should now bring more light to your boards.

  • Aurelion Sol Non-Mech Spell Damage: 320/480 AP ⇒ 335/505 AP
  • Karma Split Damage AP: 570/855 ⇒ 630/945
  • LeBlanc Passive Damage AP: 62/93 ⇒ 66/99
  • LeBlanc Sigil Damage: 85/130 AP ⇒ 95/145 AP
  • Morgana Health Gain AP: 525/625 ⇒ 600/700
  • Morgana Ally Heal AP: 100/150 ⇒ 125/185
  • Master Yi Spell Damage AD: 50/75 AD ⇒ 55/85 AD
  • Nami Primary Spell Damage: 440/660 AP ⇒ 460/690 AP
  • Nami Secondary Spell Damage: 110/165 AP ⇒ 125/185 AP

UNITS: TIER 5

Shen’s Attack Speed will no longer decay over the course of his ability, but he’s still mana locked so he won’t chain cast with absurdly high amounts of Attack Speed. Expect him to be more exciting as he now consistently hits faster and always buffs himself with his ability.

  • Shen will always gain his Attack Speed bonus after casting his ability, even if it does not hit himself.
  • Shen’s Attack Speed buff no longer decays when buffing Shen. Other allies receive the same decaying buff.

AUGMENTS

The bulk of our balance focus for this patch is Augments, so expect a very long list with a few highlights here.

With this pass, one of our goals is to make Augments more general and less specific to lobby shapes/builds. Things like Best Friends I/II—which previously only granted Armor—now gets both Armor and Magic Resist, while Blood Offering will also grant AP in addition to AD, making it a solid take for AP comps.

We’re also buffing many of our Augments that just haven’t been hitting the mark in terms of power. You’ll notice quite a few buffs for Augments that provide Thief’s Gloves.

On the nerf list, we’ve got some overdue nerfs for Birthday Reunion, Expedition, and Self Destruct (Gragas). We’ve also got nerfs to Restart Mission that remove its powerful interaction with open fort-style (not playing a full board to lose streak + econ) Augments that took away the tradeoff for the Augment.

We’ve opted to disable Critical Success, which in most cases was very weak and sometimes never cashed out. But in situations where you could build a bunch of crit items early, it could provide a fast and powerful spike. Overall, the Augment required too specific of a set up to be worth rebalancing.

We moved Loot Singularity’s (Dark Star) cashouts around to grant components earlier and keep it on pace with other Gold Augments. We also reworked the final cashout and removed the impossible-to-achieve ones, but Cashout 16 will be VERY hard to hit.

  • Loot Singularity:
    • Cashouts 17-20 removed

PENGU’S PARTY

Demacia, Honeymancy, and Storyweaver Kayle have all been partying a little too hard this anniversary, so as to avoid them not getting an invite for Pengu’s next party, we’re going to nerf them here and keep the sustainable (and balanced) party vibes going. We've also got some buffs to some underperforming Anniversary traits that haven't quite been able to get into the party spirit!

We also have a few bugfixes for Pengu’s Party. Notably one for the 920 and 1000 Ixtal cashouts that should now provide their promised powerful rewards.
